articles.title: Agnikarma Shalaka
articles.excerpt:
Agnikarma shalaka
A probe is needed to perform the Agnikarma Chikitsa. Various conditions require use of different types of probes. The temperature of the probe
articles.content:
Agnikarma shalaka
A probe is needed to perform the Agnikarma Chikitsa. Various conditions require use of different types of probes. The temperature of the probe too is decided depending on the type of probe and condition of disease in the patient.

 Types:
 Suvarna shalaka i.e. gold probe.
 70% gold, 30% silver and copper in traces.
 Dimensions: Length- 7cm, Weight- 3-4g, 

 Loha shalaka i.e. iron probe.
 Dimensions: Length- 25cm.

 Panchaloha shalaka i.e. probe made out of 5 metals.
 Description: Panchaloha used are- iron, copper, silver, gold and brass.

 Jambavaushtha shalaka.
 Shara shalaka.
 Asthi.
 Godanta.
 Aja shakrut.
 Madhu.
 Guda.
 Mrittika shalaka i.e. mud probe.
 Sneha.
 Bhallatak i.e. Semicarpus anacardium.
 Pippali i.e. Pipper longum.
 Halkunda.

 Temperatures:
To perform Agnikarma, the probe should be heated. The following temperatures were used by Vd. R. B. Gogate sir in his practice-
 Pippali- 57°C, heated directly.
 Halkunda- 80°C, heated directly.
 Suvarna shalaka- 98°C-100°C, heated indirectly.
 Loha shalaka- 228°C, heated directly.
 Guda- 60°C, heated directly.
 Bhallatak- 54°C, heated directly.
 Mrittika shalaka- 80°C- 100°C, heated directly.

 Use of various shalakas:
 Pippali, aja shakrut, godanta, shara shalaka can be used with respect to skin.
 Pippali and halkunda can be used in conditions related to yakrit and pleeha and kamala as well as skin.
 Panchaloha shalaka can be used in mamsa vrana.
 Jambavaushtha shalaka can be used in mamsa vrana.
 Use of guda can be seen in Avabahuk.
 Use of madhu, ghrita and sneha is seen in sira, snayu, asthiand sandhivrana.
 Use of mrittika shalaka can be seen in calcaneal spur and kurchashoola.

articles.title: Viddhakarma and it's Correlation with Chinese medicine
articles.excerpt:
Introduction to Viddha karma
Viddha karma is mentioned in Ayurveda for instant pain management.
It is a sterile procedure in which specific points are pierced o
articles.content:
Introduction to Viddha karma
Viddha karma is mentioned in Ayurveda for instant pain management.
It is a sterile procedure in which specific points are pierced or punctured using disposable hollow Viddha needles.
Viddha karma is performed on specific points with all precautions to avoid injury to marma.
Viddha karma is performed superficially or deep on the affected part of patient’s body according to patient’s tolerance and severity of pain.

Correlation with Chinese medicine
Chinese and Ayurvedic medicines are contemporary. Indonesia is also related by cultural bonds with India and neighbouring countries since last many centuries and hence the traditional therapeutic medicines developed in this region are having a quite close resemblance with each other. There are definite proofs that various types of exchanges in many respects was a routine practice during that era.
One similar principle applied in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine is – Ushna and sheeta. This is applied in both the external and internal regimens. The equilibrium of both these elements is equal to health and derangement means disease. This is basic theme of both the sciences.
Because of the fear of over description, many descriptions in Ayurvedic texts are quite brief and need explanation with the help of other sciences as per Ayurveda’s advice.
It was heard that Viddha chikitsa and Agni chikitsa are practiced in Chinese medicine. But it was not practiced in India. This was the outcome of bias minded international policies of British government, whereby, in view of promoting allopathic pharmaceutical products, the therapies like Viddha and Agni karma lagged behind as compared to china.
Hence, for analysing the claims made by other similar sciences, I retrieved the literature related to Chinese acupuncture and Moxibustion from the publications of Chinese government and studied them at depth twice. It was noted that both the sciences have several similarities. Ayurveda has quoted very few sites for Viddha for many ailments to relieve pain.
Following points are worth noting while considering the similarities between both the sciences;
1. Both have stated Anguli pramana. It is to be taken in relation to every individual patient. Surface anatomy is important here.
2. There is clear explanation in the Chinese medicine while measuring the points horizontally as well as vertically.
3. Ayurveda has advised Viddha chikitsa for the conditions like Aavrita/Margavrodhaja vata, collected fluid substances like in mutravriddhi, dakodara, pooya from vidradhi (Asthigata vata, Asthi vidradhi) or vitiated blood. Chinese acupuncture has advised on the same line.
4. For Agni karma, Ayurveda has stated use of plant products like Pimpali, Bibba, Harida, Jaggery etc. Chinese medicine has used garlic, Davana and likewise for Moxibustion.
5. Chinese medicine has advised iron needle rod for Agni karma, while Ayurveda has advised pancha dhatu shalaka.
6. Ayurveda has advised Agni karma for non recurrence of tumours. This is not mentioned in Chinese medicine.
7. Ayurveda has duly considered the marma points while implementing Agni karma, which has not been mentioned by Chinese medicine.
8. Moxibustion has been advised for ailments due to shaitya(coldness) in Chinese therapy, which is similar in the case of Ayurveda.
9. Viddha chikitsa has been advocated in the diseases due to vitiation of vata in both the sciences.
10. Ayurveda advocated Agni karma where Viddha is not beneficial. In Chinese medicine Moxibustion has been advised at many places after acupuncture.
11. Whenever the pathogenesis is related to Snayu – sandhi, the procedures like snehana, Swedana, Agni karma and Viddha Chikitsa are to be performed repeatedly. Chinese science has advocated the same thing.
The Viddha and Agni karma sites are same in Ayurveda and Chinese medicine. But Ayurveda has avoided naming them by personal characters, while Chinese medicine has given names of scholars. Following are some of the examples:
Viddha sthana per Ayurveda and same point by Chinese medicine with a name:
1. जिव्हा मूले व्यधेत Vuve, Jinjng
2. उपनासिके – नासासमीपे Bitong, Vingxiang
3. ललाट्यां नासाग्रे Ygngbai, Moxibustion application.
4. भ्रृपुच्छे Si Zhukong.
5. हनुसंधिमध्यग Xiaguan, Moxibustion application
6. नासाग्रे Daheng, sulioo – Moxibustion application.
 The points noted for Viddha are same for Agni karma. And I utilize them without any complication in practice.
Ayurveda has presented Ushna and sheeta principles primarily. Ushna has an upward tendency while sheeta has downward tendency. (Agni and Jala)
As per Chinese science, the upward part of body is Yang (heat) and lower part is Yin (cold)
Ayurveda has stated 20 guna but there are 10 principle guna and remaining 10 as their deficient. (Opposite guna) The dominance of one overrides its Opposite guna. E.g. – if Ushna is dominant, Sheeta is dominated or vice – a – versa.
Although, the pathological changes that occur in disease are complicated, they can be generalized and explained by imbalance of Yin and Yang.
Excess of Yin – Cold syndrome.
Excess of Yang – Heat syndrome.
Deficiency of Yin – Heat syndrome.
Deficiency of Yang – Cold syndrome.
Reference: Chinese medicine.
This discussion leads to clarify that both the sciences have a similar view regarding the basic principles monitoring our body as well as its therapeutic principles. It is debatable issue, who transferred this knowledge to whom or both were the same country during a certain period; this is a subject of the specialist in the concerned field.
The deranged status of Ushna and Sheeta guna can be corrected within a short time, without giving any medicines like NSAIDs and very economical with the help of Agni karma and Viddha Chikitsa. This achieves instant pain relief.
I expect that every practitioner should follow these therapeutic measures. It was decided by me not to write any book without completing 5000 patients. Which has been achieved now without any complication.
Hence it is requested to rejuvenate all this therapeutics at a wider level and make Ayurveda everlasting. Nevertheless, Ayurveda is itself everlasting.

articles.title: Viddhakarma points 1
articles.excerpt:
VIDDHAKARMA POINTS 1

In practice, one question always comes in our mind is, is there any treatment in Ayurveda to stop the pain immediately. No one has shown t
articles.content:
VIDDHAKARMA POINTS 1

In practice, one question always comes in our mind is, is there any treatment in Ayurveda to stop the pain immediately. No one has shown to us and we have never seen such treatment. But in my professional career of so many years I can assure you that Ayurveda has such treatment to stop the pain immediately.
This treatment of pain relief is described by Sushruta in chapter of Viddha chikitsa. Of course he has described that wherever raktamokshan is not possible (Blood letting) you can go for Viddha chikitsa (To bore a hole to drain). SO this Viddha chikitsa is also used in various diseases other than pain treatment, For Example: to drain the accumulated fluid in Jatodak awastha (Ascites), to let out entrapped vaayu in circulation of blood vessels, to let out pus in vidradhi (abscess).
When Viddha chikitsa is used for pain relief, then different measurements are described according to site of pain. If blood vessel is clearly visible at the site described then raktamokshan should be done first, as described by Ayurveda. But site like ear nose where blood vessels are not clearly visible, we have to do Viddha chikitsa. Viddha word has meaning ‘deep wound’. When we have to let accumulation from the site, then this wound should be hollow. The needle we use for siravyadha is also hollow instrument. When we do raktamokshan for pain relief by siravyadh we use blood pressure instrument to assist us. Text describes that such site should be tied or such site should be kept hanging. But instead of this, cuff of BP instrument acts as a good tourniquet to give pressure on the vein and make it clearly visible. It helps to monitor blood pressure also because if blood pressure falls bellow 90 mmHg systolic then there are chances of gangrene, especially when we perform siravyadh at the site with very small finger like capillaries. Medico legally it is very important to monitor gangrene like side-effects during siravyadh.

After draining, do not stop the oozing blood immediately. Let it come out side naturally. And wait for it to stop naturally. During this process we can monitor the positive blood pressure. After blood stops completely we remove the needle. Hence taking all these aspects into consideration, it is very useful to use BP instrument for siravyadh in present era.
It is useful in aspect of patient as well as the doctor.

In siravyadh and Agni karma treatment Viddha chikitsa is performed first and then followed by Agnikarma. Even in texts same pattern is described. Reason behind this is; Agni karma is indicated in severe pain but in diseases like sciatica, frozen shoulder, pain is present in large area, in such area it is difficult to perform Agni karma and patient refuses to perform it at many sites.

In such cases, all points where Viddha chikitsa is indicated we can perform Agnikarma & it has been proved to be fruitful. In Ayurveda, treatments advised to relieve pain include Snehan, Swedan, mardan, bandhan, Viddha and then Agnikarma. So inference can be drawn that if pain is not relieved by Viddha chikitsa then perform Agnikarma for pain relief. And it is seen in practice that when pain is not relieved by Viddha in that case Agnikarma is seen to be useful. When we perform Viddha chikitsa raktamokshan is the first choice. Principle behind this is after Viddha impure blood come out first which is cause of disease. For Viddha chikitsa, Ayurveda has described different types of needles, length of such needle is described as ‘Yavamatra’ or ‘Vrihimatra’ commonly, it appears to be 11 to 13 mm. In ancient time ‘Aara’ instrument was used for this purpose. But now it is difficult to use such instruments. Practically it is difficult for patient to sustain, hence we use needle for this purpose. Insulin needle has exact measurement of 11mm in length and 0.45 mm in breadth. So we can achieve exact Viddha up to Yava, Vrihi, Ardha Vrihi proportion. (It comes approx. 4-6 mm as 1 Yava or Vrihi. and 2-4 mm as ½ Yava or Vrihi) insulin needle is used for Viddha. We can use it to relieve pain up to mamsa dhatu. This needle produces very little amount of blood letting, so patient doesn’t get frightened. After practice, we can use this needle to make Viddha at the base of tongue at palate. For newcomers it is little difficult to use such needle to perform Viddha at such places. Hence such newcomer Doctors should use insulin needle to perform such Viddha. There are indications for how deep we should prick the needle. For Example: When pain or tingling present only in skin, then Viddha should be performed up to the skin level.

When disease in mamsa dhatu, we perform Viddha little deep so as to reach up to mansa dhatu. This is generally up to ¼ vrihi and when we have to perform it up to bone, vessels, tendon, then full 1 vrihi Viddha should be performed which is deeper. In obese patient, insulin needle is not so much useful. Needle no 24 is used in such cases. This needle should be used carefully.
When insulin needle is small, it is very safe for the patients.

Ayurveda has described various points for Viddha. But even if we make Viddha nearby these points it is also very useful. Viddha chikitsa should not be performed on small children, pregnant women, old persons. Though these people are contraindicated for Viddha as per texts, we can perform Viddha by using instruments which we use now. As these instruments are very safe and do not create any side effects in these people. Only problem occurs in small children is that they do not sit in required proper position of Viddha. Hence it becomes difficult to perform Viddha in them. But we can perform Viddha in pregnant women and old people very neatly. As stated earlier, because of safe instruments we can perform Viddha in these people without any complications. This is my routine experience.
Viddha or raktamokshan is contraindicated in following environmental conditions; namely cloudy weather, during rain and at night. Though these contraindications are described in texts, we can perform Viddha even in these conditions with the help of some artificial assistance. These natural conditions don’t create any hazard for us. But it is observed that Viddha performed in such natural conditions doesn’t get well performed. In cold conditions, Viddha is not fully achieved. In spite of all this we can perform Viddha in such conditions without any complications.
When patient is in acute condition, we should not consider these contraindications. Viddha or Agni karma should be performed immediately. For example: colicky pain, appendicitis pain, severe headache. In emergency conditions Viddha can be done immediately without any poorva karma. For example: pain in abdomen, colicky pain, pain in appendicitis. If we don’t perform Viddha or Agni karma in such conditions, there are chances of severe complications. Hence Viddha or Agni karma Is immediately performed.
In chronic diseases, Viddha or Agni karma has to be performed many times. For example: chronic pain in sciatica, lumbago, cervical spondylosis, etc. When pain in such diseases is long standing, then Viddha or Agni karma should be done many times. In such cases it should be performed at evening, on next day morning and again in the evening. When Viddha or Agni karma is repeated in such way, patient definitely gets relief. As per text, Viddha should be followed by Agni karma in some conditions. but This rule is not for every situation. specially in headache, nasal disorders Viddha should be followed by Agni karma as per text. Again this description is not mentioned in text for every situation but points of Viddha and Agni karma are same. Generally, blunt probe of gold (Suvarna Shalaka) is used for Agni karma.

articles.title: Viddhakarma points 2
articles.excerpt:
Part 2 ( with agnikarma tips!)
We use Suvarna Shalaka because needle can not be used in diabetic patients. As it doesn’t cause wound, so pus formation is natura
articles.content:
Part 2 ( with agnikarma tips!)
We use Suvarna Shalaka because needle can not be used in diabetic patients. As it doesn’t cause wound, so pus formation is naturally prevented. Of course it is used in pain only. When there is pain of calcaneal spur, then Mrittika Shalaka is used. (Mud or clay probe) 
In case of corn, heated Loh Shalaka (Iron probe) is used. This probe should not be too pointed. This probe should be red hot for Agni karma success. If it is not so much hot, then there are chances of pus formation. And wound takes much more time to heal and corn is also not cured. So, not too pointed but red hot Iron probe is must while performing this Agni karma. 
Agni karma is used to relieve pain as well as to cure the disease. Texts reveal that diseases cured by Agni karma never recur. Hence after excision of tumour, Agni karma is done at operated site for prevention of recurrence. In Ayurveda Agni karma has been used to stop bleeding (Rakta stambhan). In excessive bleeding, Agni karma is done at bleeding site. Of course it is the last remedy to stop bleeding when treatments like binding (Sandhan), coagulation (Skandan), pachan are not working. Ayurveda was completely aware that When Agni karma was done to stop bleeding, bleeding stops but normal tissues at that site get damaged. Hence Agni karma is stated as the last choice to stop the bleeding. Cautery which is similar to Agni karma is commonly used in all operatives. If Cautery is done after hernia operation, then chances of recurrence are more. Because Cautery damages normal tissues at that site. 
Modern scientists warned about this but surgeons ignored this fact. Surgeons use coagulation Cautery to save time, no need to ligate each and every blood vessel, mopping of blood is less required. Surgeons compromise by doing coagulation Cautery. But in case of hernia, recurrence is more after such Cautery. In case of TUR (Trans Urethral Resection), obstructive pathology is seen after use of such Cautery. Thus Agni karma is used for various purposes. Today we are restricted to it's use only in pain relief. 


The fact is also applied to Viddha Chikitsa. Generally, Rakta mokshan is done in Rakta Pradoshaj vikara (Blood disorders). Blood letting is done if blood pressure is increased suddenly. Viddha or Rakta mokshan is done to cure many diseases. 
Viddha or Agni karma is needed many times. It is described that we can perform treatments till patient can tolerate and doesn’t go in shock. Patient and doctor both should be alert, conscious during these procedures. Because of logistic problems, patient can not come frequently or twice a day. Hence by experience we perform these procedures for seven days. Because during procedures many times wound is created. And wound or burn or Viddha takes time of seven days to heal. Our treatment should give relief to patient in 7 days is other aspect of this. Jaggery is also used for Agni karma. But such material should be used at specific points. For example: muscular wasting of shoulder (Ansa shosha), frozen shoulder (Avabahuka) where Jaggery is recommended. Cow tooth (Godanta) is also recommended like Jaggery. In such cases, when there is no specific mention of Agni karma material then in that case, by experience Pancha Dhatu (5 metals namely Gold, Silver, Copper, Iron, Brass) are used as material. In many colleges, Shalaka (probe) made up of all 5 dhatus is used. But our body parts respond to different temperatures. Hence all these metals should be used separately as this gives better results. 
In Shalakya Tantra (E.N.T) Viddha Chikitsa is predominantly used. This Viddha Chikitsa includes almost 50% treatment in E.N.T than other treatments described. Sushruta described this treatment first. 500 years after Sushruta, Vagbhata also described this treatment in E.N.T. Interestingly, Vagbhata made changes in Rasayan Chikitsa if compared to Sushruta. But description of Viddha Chikitsa, points of Viddha are same as stated by Sushruta. It shows this was routinely practised in between period of these 2 stalwarts. In spite of dominance of Bauddha Dharma in era of Vagbhata, this Viddha Chikitsa was in great practice. 

If someone asks me whether this treatment was only in India or any other country? Answer is Yes. Our neighbouring country China has such treatment in the name of acupuncture and moxibustion. These are very similar to Viddha and Agni karma Chikitsa respectively. In acupressure also, triangular needles were used in ancient time which are similar to our ‘Aara’ instrument. During the course of time changes occurred and now a days generally Platinum needles are used. Depth of Viddha mentioned by Ayurveda is same as stated in acupuncture. 
Whether moxibustion should be done after acupuncture?  Is mentioned after each procedure in Chinese medicine. Ayurveda doesn't have such specific instructions. Both these sciences are developed in same era approximately 1500 B.C. Both nations have geographical similarities. i.e. Both have hilly region like Himalaya on one side and sea on the other side. Ayurveda accepts sheeta (Cold) and Ushna (Hot) as basic principles. Chinese medicine also has same principle in the name of Yin (Cold) and Yang (Hot). So Chinese medicine and Ayurveda are that way same. WHO has given recommendation as ‘medical treatment’ to acupressure and moxibustion. Ayurveda has covered Viddha and Agni karma Chikitsa in less points as compared to acupressure and moxibustion. It actually denotes Ayurveda's Greatness. But unfortunately this science doesn't get its true value. 
Viddha and Agni karma were fully used in practice in surgery as well as in E.N.T still it is not recognised in world today. We give reason of Bauddha religion for it but This reason is not logical. In spite of Bauddha religion dominance, accidents, foreign body intrusion, animal attacks were routine happenings in that era also. Where treatment was necessary. 

Stambha means muscular spasm. Vat (Vayu) is entrapped in muscles and hence there are restrictions to the movements. In such cases, Agni karma is performed after doing Snehan (Massage) and Swedan (Fomentation). This gives better results in cervical muscle spasm. Pradhaman Nasya is done before Agni karma which gives better results. For this Pradhaman Nasya, Nebasulf powder bottle is used. Such bottle has very small hole so it becomes easy to inhale the powder inside. For Pradhaman, mixed powder of Vacha (Acorus) and suntha (Ginger) is used in proportion of 2/3 and 1/3 respectively. Such bottles are easily available and very comfortable to use. Medicinal powder is inhaled in proper quantity. 
Another similarity between Ayurveda and Chinese medicine is when disease is caused by cold principle in that case Agni karma is used and Viddha is used in cases of diseases caused by hot principle. Hence near seashore acupressure or Viddha are more fruitful than Himalaya region and vice a versa, moxibustion or Agni karma is more fruitful in Himalaya region as compared to seashore. So hot and cold principles are used in these treatments. Ayurveda has not stated this clearly but Chinese medicine has such clear description. In China, in Himalaya region Agni karma is done and near seashore acupuncture is performed. In normal climate region like Pune, we will not find such difference. But in cold places like Kashmir, Viddha will not be fruitful as blood will not come out because of cold weather. Main condition in Agni karma is obstructive pathology is cured and pain inducing factors get assimilated in blood. Thus pain is relieved. Exact action of Viddha is not known but as stated in Rakta mokshan, impure blood lets out first. Vayu is also of Laghu Guna and pain is always because of Vayu. So after Rakta mokshan or Viddha, this Vayu escapes out and pain is relieved. In science of Ayurveda, this treatment is immortal. Ayurveda has mentioned another important thing. like earth, our body has 80% water content and 20% solid content. Hence considering dominance of Udak (Jala/water) principle, Agni karma is more recommended.

articles.excerpt:

2 precautions should be taken before doing Viddha or Rakta mokshan. First thing is check if patient gets frightened by seeing blood. If it is so, then we
articles.content:
Part 3
2 precautions should be taken before doing Viddha or Rakta mokshan. First thing is check if patient gets frightened by seeing blood. If it is so, then we have to perform the procedures carefully in such a way that patient doesn't see blood. Another thing to be asked before Viddha or Agni karma check if patient went into shock after taking any injection or any prick. If such history is present, then both these procedures should be done very carefully. Amount of blood letting should not go above 250 ml. Though Ayurveda says 560 ml blood can be withdrawn but it is not accepted. We should stick to standard parameters about the blood amount accepted worldwide. There is one difference between Viddha of Ayurveda and acupuncture of Chinese medicine, needle should be retained at that place, it should be removed inside – such descriptions are seen in acupuncture. But no such descriptions in Ayurveda.
Now we will see where to make Viddha at different sites. First of them is Viddha should be done at lateral side of nose. It is done for diseases of eyes, forehead. It is done specially to relieve pain. It is also useful in sinusitis. It is done for ½ Vrihi at maximum depth. Generally, this Viddha if done at right angle of skin, it is more beneficial. Next Viddha is on forehead. No specific point on forehead is described in Ayurveda. In practice, we choose point of acupuncture. This point is at lower 1/3rd of forehead and last 1/3rd of eyebrows. It is also used to relieve pain in all shiro rog. Viddha is done above Apang marma where hairline starts or ends. Used in diseases of eyes and forehead. Viddha at Hanu sandhi is very useful in apasmar (Epilepsy) it is done for ½ Vrihi depth. In apasmar, along with Viddha, treatment suggested by Dr. Y.G. Joshi is also advised. It includes rice kept on pimpal leaves (Ficus religiosa) is given to patient. Both these treatments give magnificent results to reduce attacks in Apasmar. Viddha is done behind ear lobule at two places. One at the start of ear lobule on upper side. And one on lower side below 2 anguli (approx. 4cm) below Vidhur marma near hairline. It reduces earache immediately. Tinnitus is also relieved by this Viddha. This Viddha is specifically mentioned in ‘Tandra' (Drowsiness). Viddha at the top of nose is useful in anosmia. Also useful in all nasal disorders like sinusitis, rhinitis, deviated nasal septum is reduced by this Viddha. For better results Ghrita is applied over nose.
Viddha at palate is done to reduce upper teeth pain. It also reduces coughing due to elongated uvula. It reduces elongated uvula. Viddha at palate is done at the border of anterior 2/3rd and posterior 1/3rd of the palate.
Viddha is done at the root of tongue at lateral side of lingual veins. It stops lower teeth pain. Right side Viddha reduces pain of side. Similarly, true for left side. When pathology is all over mouth then Viddha on both sides is performed. For example: diseases like slurred speech, mouth ulcers, glossitis. Viddha is done 2 anguli (4cm) above Kshipra marma. It is done at both limbs and depth is more than ½ Vrihi. This Viddha is used in severe burning, pain, loss of sensation at hands and feet. Also useful in cracked foot, ankle sprain, tingling in feet.
For wrist pain, Viddha is done 4 anguli (8cm) above wrist joint. Or this Viddha is done in Vishwachi (Brachial neuritis). Depth is more than ½ Vrihi but less than 1 Vrihi.
Viddha is suggested above and below elbow joint used in elbow joint pain. For Vishwachi It is done below elbow joint. Important thing is all these Viddha on limbs are to be done laterally.
Viddha is done 4 anguli (8cm) below and left side of umbilicus is Useful in pain in abdomen. Also used to tap fluid in ascites. Depth of this Viddha is specifically mentioned in the texts. It is above thumb length. Of course it is not practically possible in today’s time. Maybe this measurement was described according to physical status of people at that time. So pain in abdomen is reduced by this Viddha and ascitic fluid tapping is done by this.
In Ayurveda, points of Viddha for Tritiyak jwara (A type of fever) and chaturthak jwar (A type of fever) are mentioned. But these type of fevers are not found in present days so these points are long forgotten. Still for information, For Tritiyak jwara Viddha is done at the centre of Trika sandhi. This point is below the Spinous process of fifth lumbar vertebra. And for chaturthak jwara, Viddha should be done in mid axillary line or posterior and inferior to the shoulder joint when arm is adducted. It is on posterior axillary fold. For ankle sprain, Elephantiasis Viddha is done 4 anguli (8cm) above ankle joint. Depth is 1 Vrihi. Ankle pain is relieved by this Viddha.
Viddha below 2 anguli of Indrabasti marma is done in both limbs. It is done for Lymph node enlargement (Gandamala) in upper limb and if present in hip area, then Viddha is done in lower limb. Agni karma is followed by this Viddha. For sciatica, Viddha is done below ankle joint 4 anguli laterally.
Medial to right elbow joint, Viddha is done for liver disorders. And for spleen disorders, it is done medial to left elbow joint. Here Rakta mokshan is suggested through veins in this area. As Rakta mokshan is more beneficial than Viddha. This is the only Viddha point on medial side as all others in the limbs are on lateral side.
In hydrocele, Viddha is done below and lateral side at testis. Depth is not mentioned but puncture it till Urine is seen. For shukra Dhatu disorders, Viddha should be done on penis. But in practice instead of Viddha Jaloukavacharan is done in this area.

articles.excerpt:
Part 4
There is confusion regarding position of penis. Weather it should be erected or not. If modern science is considered, the position of penis is more suita
articles.content:
Part 4
There is confusion regarding position of penis. Weather it should be erected or not. If modern science is considered, the position of penis is more suitable for Viddha. Specifically, in leukaemia patients, there is symptom of priapism. In such cases, Rakta Mokshan is advised on upper part by taking marking incisions. In calcaneal spur, mud probe (Mrittika Shalaka) is used for Agni karma. In calcaneal spur, Agni karma is performed at the point with severe pain. This Shalaka should be blunt and not pointed. When this Shalaka is heated on candle light, then small paper is kept on Agni karma point because carbon formed by candle light flame can cause wound at Agni karma point. Also if these carbon particles are not removed completely then there are chances of cancer at that point. Hence this precaution of keeping paper is must when candle is used for heating the Shalaka. But when stove or gas is used for heating then this precaution is not needed. In Apachi (Cervical lymphadenitis) above wrist joint 3 lines are said to be drawn by heated Shalaka with distance of 1 anguli (2cm) between them. Agni karma is suggested to perform at the base of the thumb (anatomical snuff box). This Agni karma is specifically done in jaundice and for this Agni karma turmeric is used after heating it. In this Agni karma, dushtavrana is expected. This treatment is done on upadhatu of Rakta Dhatu i.e. sira (vessel) and kandara (tendons). Treatment on upadhatu is mentioned first time in this Agni karma.
Agni karma is done at painful points we can do it at any painful point. Only consider that this is not ‘marma’ (vital) point. While performing Viddha or Agni karma, we need to fix the points. Many times anguli praman is described to fix the points. Sometimes marma points are also described to fix points of Agni karma and Viddha. Hence knowledge of marma points is very important before performing these procedures. Anguli praman is considered to be most important measure to fix points. In Chinese medicines acupressure and moxibustion also anguli praman is stated.
Description of anguli praman by Ayurveda and Chinese medicines is almost similar. Generally, distance at 1st interphalangeal joint of index finger is considered as ‘anguli praman' or distance between joined four fingers is said to be ‘four angulis’. This distance divided by four or two is considered to be 1 anguli or 2 anguli. This distance is to be measured according to patient's fingers. These distance criteria are now fixed for that patient. This distance is measured in centimetres and then used in Viddha or Agni karma for fixation of point. For example: 4 anguli above ankle joint, 2 anguli below Indrabasti marma, 2 anguli below Vidhur marma, Etc.

articles.content:
SHALAKYA TANTRA AT A GLANCE

The diseases in the urdwa Jatrugata Pradesh (Area above the manubrum sterni) are grouped under the subclass of shalakyatantra . This Urdhwa Jatrugat Pradesh includes the structure like Nasa (Nose) , Karna (ear), Netra(Eyes) , Mukh(Mouth) which includes Jiwha (Tongue), Kantha(Oropharynx) and Shir (Crenium with Contents) Mastulunga (Brain)
The main cause in separating these diseases, a Tantra, called as “Shalakyatantra” (Different types of probes) are used, for diagnosis & curative purpose. Different types of Vyuhan Yantras (Scopes) are also used esp. for ear,nose & oropharynx.
For example
1)To determine the depth of danta nadi (dental sinus) the probe is used as diagnostic instrument. 2) For application of medicines in the eyes ‘Anjana shalaka’ issued. 3) For removing Karna Goothak Karna Vishodhani shalaka is used. 4) For dahankarma-again heated probe is used. 5) For application of tailas, quathas or for cleaning the wounds a shalaka called as Karpasa Krutashanisha shalaka is used.
For karna & Nasa Auroscope, Nasal Speculum (Talayantra) and oroscope is used to remove Foreign Bodies. (H§$R>gº$ eë¶)
Health of the body depends upon the good health of the indriyas, namely Netra, Nasa, Karna, Mukha, Twak and Shir. They are responsible for reception of Dhyana and have a separate storing capacity as netrabudhi (olfactory lobes) brocas area (olfactory bulb). Shir holds the prime importance
If Shir and its allied organs are in a good healthy condition, then the body growth and its maintenance is good.
In day to day life it is commonly seen that the person who cannot either see, smell or lacks the sense of taste cannot rally be called healthy though overall he may present a healthy picture with no obvious problrms. Such a person however cannot lead a smoother life and his movements or his getting about in Life is Limited to a certain extent. Therefore need arises for us to diagnose and treat the symptoms or the group of symptoms (Disease) as described in shalakya tantra and see to it that their normal healthy condition is restored as early as possible.
If the health of these organs is not maintained Latter develop into complications leading to loss of independence. A simple Netrabhishyand (Conjunctivitis) if not treated in time develops into (a corneal opacity) Sawranashukra ultimately produces blindness.

. PANCHABHUTIK (SHARIR) INDRIYAN.
You very well know that according to Ayurved our body is composed of principles of panchamahabhoota. Each of the Indriya in shalakya tantra represents one mahabhoota and possesses guna Gra’han of that mahabhoota.
Netra - Represent “Tejas” Mahabhoot does graham of roop
Karna - Represents “Akasha” Mahabhoot, does graham of Shabda
Nose - Represents “Prithavi” Mahabhoot, does graham of Gandha
Tongue - Represents “Apa” Mahaboot, does grahan of taste
Skin - Represents “ Vayu” Mahabhoot, does grahan of Sparsha
Normally the health of these indriyas (organs) is maintained from Poshan principles of these Mahabhootas, from the diet-the food.

. NORMALLY HABITANT DOSHAS & THEIR KARMA
Alochak Pitta - eye to see
Bodhak Kapha - mouth to taste
Sadhak Pittat - Shirastha Hridaya Dhee, medha.
Pranavayu - ura, kantha,shir,tones-up indriyas, to-spit, to talk, to swallow food, to exhale air, etc.
Udan Vayu - nasta to nabhi to talk, to intiate, gives strength to the body, luster to Skin, improves memory.
Vyan Vayu - Shirastha Hridaya. All the movements of the body including Nimesha & Unmesha of eye ball.

. FACE INFLUENCING THE PERSONALITY
The Appearance of the individual & Longevity depends largely on the appearance of his face, thus the lips nose, the eyes, forehead acquire a place of great importance. The ideal description is given below.
Oshtha (lips) - 4 Angulas in length, should not be too thick or thin, when shut, mouth Should not open.
Nasa (Nose) - 4 Angulas in length. Should be straight with tip of the nose slightly curved.
Netra (Eyes) - Both the eyes should be identical. Both the eyebrows should not meet in the centre. Eyebrows should bend downwards, big and hairy. They Should be sparkling bright.
Karna (ears) - In shalakya tantra the size of the ear assumes a great importance in Determining the span of life. The ears which are big, identical, bigger at the Lower edge (pinna) bending back with plenty of hairs will usually lead a long Life.
Fore head - 4 angulas in length (From hair line to eyebrow hair line).

. MARMAS PLAYING IMPORTANT ROLE IN SURGERY
Following Marmas are described in urdhwajatrugata Pradesh and produce the symptoms as shown against them.
1) Dhamani -- hoarness or change in voice
2) Matruka -- Death
3) Krikatika -- Shirokampa, Tossing of head
4) Vidhur -- Deafness
5) Phana --Loss of sense of smell
6) Apanga --Loss of vision or diminution of vision
7) Avarta -- Blindness
8) Shankha -- Death
9) Utkshepaka -- Impacted F.B. if removed death
10) Seemanta -- Fainting, Semiconciousness or insanity
11) Shrungataka -- Death
12) Adipati -- Death
13) Stapani -- Impacted F.B.if removed death

. SWASTHA VRITTA IN RELATION TO SHALAKYATANTRA.
Ayurved gives more importance on prevention of diseases than cure. In Swastha Vritta some measures for maintenance of good heaith of Indriyas-Netra, Karna, Nasa, Danta & Shirotwak has been described.
For good health to teeth the daily use of soft stems of herbs like Nimba,Khadir,Karanja having Kashaya astringent, Tikta (Bitter) &Katu (Pungent) taste have been advised, at the same with an advise not to injure the gums while using Dantakastha.

An individual having indigestion or sensation of vomitting should avoid Tikata rasa, Jwara(Fever) Kashaya rasa and Katu rasa, swasa & kasa-kashaya rasa.
Kaphadosha if dominate in eyes hampers the function of Alochaka Pitta. Daily use of Saviranjan prevents this & project the eyes from Kaphadosha.

. NUMBER OF DISEASES IN SHALAKYA TANTRA
Charaka, Sushrut & Wagbhat have given the following number of diseases. The diffrance in number is mainly due classifying the symptoms as diseases.
. DIAGNOSIS IN CHILDREN
Diagnosis of the diseases of mouth or the earache in infants has been accurately described.
If the child is suffering From oral diseases there will be Salivation, inability to suck, Vomitting out of Feeds, rapid breathing with alae naise moving.
If the child is having earache the child touches the painful ear, constantly nocks te head, is restless, Sleepless and lacks in appetite.

. Specific Treatment in Shalakya tantra : 
Along with the general line of treatment, specific treatment for specific organs has been described. They are called as Kriya Kalpas. Namely, 1) Nasya 2) Shirobasti 3) Karnapuran 4) Netrabasthi 5) Gandoosha 6) Kawalgraha 7) Dhoomapan
Amongst the others
1) Vaman 2) Rakata mokasha 3) Dahan 4) Shalya Karma

. Nasya Chikitsa a cure of many Shalakya diseases
Amongst the Kriyakalpas Nasya plays important role in the cure of many Shalakya diseases.
Nasa is a door entry for all shalakya diseases, namely Shir, Karna ,Netra , Mukha & Nasa. Medications through nose thus cure many diseases conditions of almost all indriyas. This Chikitasa is given especially for following conditions
1)Heavyness in head 2) Headche 3) Common Cold 4) Loss of Sense of Smell 5)Diseases of neck & throat 6) Epilepsy 7) Suryawarta 8) Aradavabhedak 9) Wasting of eye balls Snosha 10) Pain in the eyes & ears 11) Noises in the ear 12) Dryness of mouth 13) Stammering 14) Graying of hair 15) Balding 16) Wrinkling of Facial Skin.

Plastic Surgery – Twagaropan – Susharut- i.e. Ayured The Pioneer of reconstruction of surgery of nose & ears.
Facial Surgery - also the first cocept in surgery in pedicle grafts. Accepted by modern plastic surgeons.
In olden days due to injuries in war, or attacks of wild animals on the individual or as a punishment by king/head of the group, problems such as torn loubles, Injuries nose or cut nose and Facial deformities in general were common .
These deformities were the problem in keeping the individuals away from the society. Deformity becomes Manoshalkya for them.
In such conditions skin grafting – the pedicle grafts were done to reconstruct the deformity. This was practiced by vaidyas of Sushrut School.

“LEGEND SHALAKI ,” HEXAGENARIAN
A GREAT ACADEMICIAN,
CALLED PROF. R. B. GOGTE
A “Great ACADEMICIAN,” “SKILLED SURGEON,”
“GENUINE TEACHER,” “DISIPLINESD ADMINISTRATOR,” “ABLE GUIDE,” “A PHILOSOPHER” &A MATURED THINKER,” called prof. Dr. R.B. Gogte was born in 1933 at a remote place in Raigad District of Maharashtra state.
Dr. Gogte got his graduation (G.F.A.M.) & THEN POST Graduation (A.V.P.)in the subject Shalya – Shalakya tantra and surgery from Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya which was affiliated to Tilak Mharashtra Vidyapeeth.
After getting enriched in practical surgery at Seth Tarachand Hospital , Dr. R. B. Gogte joined a Hospital called “Matrumandir” at Devarukh, Dist. Rantnagiri in capacity of chief Medical and administrative officer. Dr. Gogte worked with great devotion at this rural place to attain blessings from the people as “GOD MAN”
Since Dr. R. B. Gogte is a born teacher, he returned from Devarukh to join Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya as a lecture in the department of shalya shalakya. Simultaneously he was also appointed as a chief Medical officer and Deuty Superintendent of Seth Tarachand Hospital. During his services at Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya , he worked in all capacities , from Lecturer to professor, Post Graduate guide for A.V.P., M.S.(Ayu.)., M.A.Sc.Ph.d. in the subjects Shalya & Shalakyatantra . He was guide to so many students who have now become reputed surgeons.
To his credit there a number of books but special mention is required for his books, “Shalyantantra- part 1&2 ,4,” “Asthibhagna” which are accepted as reference books by various Universities.
During the career, Prof. Dr. Gogate conducted various Research projects successfully. To mention a few, they are “Kadar & Agnikarm,” “Sadyovan & Yashtimadhughut,” “Sadyovran & “vrandhooan,” “AIDS”.HIS project, namely “AIDS & AYURVED.”
Dr. R. B. Gogte was also designed in various capacities at Pune Unversity. He was a member of Academic council, Member of Ayurvedic faculty and Chairman & a member of board of studies in shalya- shalakya.
A Recipient of “Dhanvantari Puraskar” of Baidyanath , “vd. Bapurao Patwardhan Sushant Puraskar” of vd. Khadiwale Sansodhan Sanstha & “Award for Research work” by Gayatri Ayurvedic Sanshodhan Sanstha , Prof. Dr. R.B. Gogate will be felicitated with “LEGEND SHALAKI” AWARD IN “UPDATE SHALAKYATANTRA 2002” Conference .

about.title: About Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation
about.intro:
Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation is a website with a sole motto: Propagation of knowledge. This is a platform to share our grandfather’s, Vd. Ramchandra Ballal Gogate’s work and carry forward his vision ‘knowledge for all’. We are creating this platform as an authentic source of information. Our purpose is to ignite young minds through his writings and teachings. We plan to reach out to all vaidyas, students of Ayurved as well as disseminating the knowledge across all pathies and common people. Fortunately, our family has been blessed with renowned vaidyas for many generations.

Starting from Vd. Mahadev (Bapu) Gogate who was the rajavaidya to the king of Jawhar, next generation being Vd. Vishnu Mahadev Gogate (Dravyaguna) and Vd. Trimbak Mahadev Gogate (Panchakarma), next generation being Vd. Ramchandra Ballal Gogate (Shalya tantra), and this legacy still continues. They have made huge contributions to the field of Ayurved of which many remain under appreciated. This website is in their honor and remembrance. We intend to pass on the wisdom of these great professors. Vd. R. B. Gogate will always inspire us, not only as a grandfather but also through his lifetime of study, work and research.

We, his grandchildren on behalf of the Gogate family are creating this platform to promote our grandfather’s lifetime work and for our strong passion towards the field of Ayurved. We would definitely love to have your suggestions, guidelines and support in our endeavour!

Regards,
the grandchildren of Vd. R. B. Gogate, on behalf of the Gogate family

legacy.title: The Legacy of Vaidya R. B. Gogate
legacy.intro: Vd. Ramchandra Ballal Gogate — Vaidya Ramchandra Ballal Gogate — was born on 4th February 1933 at Atkar gaon and passed away on 28th September 2015 at Pune. This page shares his English biography, the Marathi remembrance by Vidula Gogate, and the posts, research and awards that still carry his work forward.
legacy.biography:
Vd. R. B. Gogate was born on 4th February, 1933 at Atkar gaon and passed away on 28th September, 2015 at Pune. He received his GFAM — General Fellow of Ayurvedic Medicine (BOM) — and AVP — Ayur Vidya Parangat in Shalya-Shalakya — from Pune, the degrees for Ayurved graduation and post-graduation at that time. His OPD was functional till his last days.

He worked as a professor for post-graduate studies (Pune University), Director — Research and publication (Sane Guruji Arogya Kendra, Hadapsar), Principal (Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya), Hon. Surgeon and HOD (Seth Tarachand Ramnath Hospital, Pune), C.M.O. (Matru Mandir Hospital, Devrukh), C.M.O. (Seth Tarachand Ramnath Hospital, Pune), Staff casualty officer (Civil Defence, Pune), Chief of AIDS research centre (STRC Hospital, Pune) and Chief of Cancer project (Pethe Arogya Kendra, Belgaum).

He worked as a consultant for Dnyanadevi trust (Pune), National AIDS Research Institute, Strategy planning committee — Ayurved, Septical Executive officer (Government of Maharashtra) and at the Pain management clinic (C.G.S. Pune).

He had done extensive research on AIDS, cancer, Agnikarma, Viddhakarma, dhoopan chikitsa in vrana, cauterisation of corns by Ayurvedic method, and raktamokshan, to name a few. He has published various books covering a large number of subjects like AIDS, Viddha and Agnikarma, Bhagna and Asthi roga, Shalya tantra and Hasti ayurved.

His work has been recognised and awarded by many institutions. The most recent award, the Pandit Ramnarayan Sharma Award for research in Ayurved (Baidyanath), was received by his son Ar. Padmanabha Gogate at the hands of the honourable President of India Shri Ramnath Kovind. His other awards include Sushrut Puraskar (Khadiwale Vaidya Sanstha), Gayatri Pratishthan Puraskar for work on AIDS, Legend Shalaki Karyabhushan Puraskar, and Jivan Gaurav Puraskar (TAMV, RSM).

His work is still carried forward by his students at his clinic and several other locations across India.
legacy.biographyMr:
आदरणीय व वंदनीय माणसे दुर्मिळ होत असताना वैद्य रामचंद्र बल्लाळ गोगटे यांचे नाव दुर्मिळ व्यक्ती म्हणून अग्रक्रमाने व प्राधान्याने घ्यावे लागेल.

४ फेब्रुवारी १९३३ रोजी जन्मलेले वैद्य रामचंद्र गोगटे हे परमेश्वराचा अवतार घेऊन इहलोकी अवतरले असेच म्हणावे लागेल. त्यांचा एकून जीवनप्रवास पाहिल्यास त्याची प्रचिती येते. त्यांनी रामचंद्र हे नाव सार्थ केले. त्यांचे वैद्यकीय ज्ञान व कौशल्य वादातीत व सर्वश्रुत आहेच; पण ज्ञानसंपन्न असूनही निगर्वी स्वभाव, उच्चपदस्थ असून सर्वसामान्यांशी जोडलेली नाळ, हसतमुख चेहरा, सेवाभावी वृत्ती आणि विद्वत्ता असून अवघड विषय सोपा करून सांगण्याची त्यांची हातोटी ही त्यांची प्रमुख वैशिष्ट्ये सांगता येतील.

ताराचंद हॉस्पिटल मध्ये त्यांनी ज्या आपलेपणाने काम केले तसे देवरुख सारख्या ग्रामीण भागात केले. कामाप्रती निष्ठा, त्यासाठी करावे लागणारे कष्ट, जिद्द व धडाडी त्यांच्याजवळ होती. ते कार्यमग्न असताना एक ज्ञानमय तपस्वी पहात असल्यासारखे वाटे. आळस हा शब्द त्यांच्या शब्दकोषात नव्हता. त्यांच्यात एवढी ऊर्जा व उत्साह कुठून येते असा प्रश्न पडत असे.

त्यांचे व्यक्तिमत्व चतुरस्त्र व बहुआयामी होते. प्रत्येक गोष्टीत परिपूर्णतेचा ध्यास व तळमळ होती. त्यांना नाट्यगीताची आवड होती व बागकामाचा छंद होता. ते रिकामे बसलेले कधी दिसत नसत. डॉक्टर लोकांचे हस्ताक्षर हा विनोदाचा विषय असताना ते मात्र अपवाद होते. त्यांचे हस्ताक्षर सुवाच्य व वळणदार होते. चित्रकलेचे अंग असल्याने रेखीव आकृत्या शोभून दिसत असत.

त्यांचे वैद्यकीय निदान व उपचार यावर त्यांच्या रुग्णांची अमाप श्रद्धा असल्याने पेशंट दुसर्‍या डॉक्टरकडे न जाता वेळ लागला तरी त्यांच्याकडेच येत असत. ते यशामागे न धावता यश त्यांच्यामागे धावत येत होते. त्यांना सुश्रुत पुरस्कार, गायत्री प्रतिष्ठान पुरस्कार, सुप्रसिद्ध शालाक्य कार्यभूषण पुरस्कार, जीवनगौरव पुरस्कार, राष्ट्रपतींच्या हस्ते दिला जाणारा पं. रामनारायण शर्मा पुरस्कार यासारख्या अनेक पुरस्कारांनी सन्मानित करण्यात आले.

आयुर्वेदिक दिनचर्या कशी योग्य आहे, निसर्गाच्या विरुद्ध जाऊन आधुनिक जीवनशैलीने व व्यसनांमुळे रोगांना आपण कसे जवळ करतो हे ते छान समजावून देत.

रक्तमोक्षण, अग्निकर्म अशा आयुर्वेदिक चिकित्सेने अनेक रोग्यांच्या जीवनात त्यांच्या दुर्धर व्याधी दूर करून आनंद फ़ुलवला. कॅन्सर रिसर्चमध्ये त्यांनी मोलाचे कार्य केले आहे. निष्णात वैद्य, तज्ञ आणि विद्यार्थीप्रिय शिक्षक असा त्यांचा लौकिक! कृतार्थ जीवन कसे जगावे याचा वस्तुपाठ त्यांनी आपल्या आचरणातून घालून दिला. त्याबद्दल आपण त्यांचे सदैव ऋणी असू. त्यांची जीवनशैली लिहिण्यास सोपी पण आचरणात आणण्यास तेवढीच अवघड.

मरावे परी कीर्तिरूपे उरावे हे त्यांच्या बाबतीत अगदी तंतोतंत खरे ठरते. ते देहरूपाने आज आपल्यात नसले तरी कार्यरूपाने आपल्यातच आहेत. त्यांच्याकडून प्रेरणा घेऊन अनेकजण आपापल्या परीने खारीचा वाटा उचलत त्यांचे कार्य पुढे नेत आहेत.

- विदुला गोगटे

anagha.title: Dr. Anagha Gogate
anagha.intro: Dr. Anagha Ramchandra Gogate (7th November 1936 – 12th September 2019) gave unwavering support and strength to Vd. Ramchandra B. Gogate.
anagha.biography:
The most significant contribution in terms of unwavering support and strength to Dr. Ramchandra B. Gogate was made by his wife, Dr. Anagha Ramchandra Gogate.

She was born on 7th November 1936 to Mr. Gajanan and Indira Sahasrabuddhe in Panchgani, Satara district of Maharashtra.

Being a daughter of a teacher father who then worked in Sanjeevan Vidyalaya school, Dr. Anagha — then called Hira — grew up in an education-friendly and constructivism-oriented environment. She did her schooling from Sanjeevan Vidyalaya, Panchgani, and moved to Pune in 1950 for her higher secondary studies in Fergusson College. She was later admitted to Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya for BAMS, where she pursued her bachelor's degree in Ayurvedic sciences. She excelled in academics all throughout her student life and thereafter.

She married Dr. Ramchandra Ballal Gogate on 21st May 1963.

She worked as an MO in Matrumandir from 1968–69 and as a clinical assistant from 1968–69. She received enormous appreciation in teaching as a professor in Tilak Ayurved Mahavidyalaya from 1970 onwards. From shifting towns with him, making all the necessary sacrifices for the family to take care of children and in-laws, giving up on ambitions and dreams, to being the strongest pillar to her husband so that he could continue to serve the people and community without any hassles and hurdles, she left no stone unturned to support him.

In spite of immense responsibilities and difficulties that she had, she continued to share his work and role as and when possible, to the best of her abilities, without a single complaint. She continued to be an epitome of love, care and resilience. We lost her on 12th September 2019 after her long-standing battle with prolonged illness. She will always be remembered for being remarkably virtuous and dutiful, with an incomparable will to stand by her husband through any odds.

PRIVACY POLICY
Last Updated: 13 November 2026

Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation respects the privacy of its customers and is committed to protecting their personal information.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store and share personal information when customers visit our website, create an account, place Normal Orders or Pre-Orders, make payments or contact our support team.

1. Information We Collect

Depending on the services used, we may collect the following information:

1.1 Personal Information
- Full name.
- Mobile number.
- Email address.
- Billing address.
- Shipping address.
- City, State and PIN code.

1.2 Order Information
- Order ID and order history.
- Books and products purchased.
- Language editions and quantities selected.
- Normal Order or Pre-Order details.
- Booking amount and remaining payment details.
- Delivery and store pickup preferences.

**1.3 Payment Information**

Payments are processed through third-party payment gateway providers.

We may receive transaction references, payment status, payment method information and other necessary transaction details.

We do not store complete credit card numbers, UPI PINs, passwords or banking credentials on our servers.

1.4 Technical Information

We may collect certain technical information, including:

- IP address.
- Browser and device information.
- Website usage information.
- Cookies and similar technologies.
- Login and security-related activity.

 2. How We Use Your Information

We use collected information for the following purposes:

- Creating and managing customer accounts.
- Processing Normal Orders and Pre-Orders.
- Confirming booking amounts and final payments.
- Reserving books and other products.
- Arranging shipping and delivery.
- Coordinating store pickups.
- Sending order confirmations and tracking updates.
- Processing cancellations, returns and refunds.
- Responding to customer enquiries and complaints.
- Preventing fraudulent transactions.
- Improving our website and services.
- Complying with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

 3. Sharing of Information

We do not sell or rent customers' personal information.

However, we may share necessary information with the following third parties:

3.1 Courier and Logistics Partners

Customer names, phone numbers and delivery addresses may be shared with courier partners to arrange shipment and delivery.

3.2 Payment Gateway Providers

Necessary transaction information may be shared with payment service providers to process payments, verify transactions and facilitate refunds.

3.3 Technology and Website Service Providers

We may use hosting providers, website infrastructure providers, communication services and technical service providers to operate and maintain our website.

3.4 Legal and Regulatory Authorities

Information may be disclosed where required by law, court orders or lawful government requests.

 4. Data Security

4.1 We take reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect personal information against unauthorised access, misuse, alteration, disclosure or loss.

4.2 Access to customer information is restricted to authorised personnel who require it for order processing and customer support.

4.3 Although we take reasonable precautions, no internet-based system can guarantee absolute security.

 5. Data Retention

5.1 We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for order fulfilment, customer support, accounting, legal compliance and dispute resolution.

5.2 Certain transaction and order records may be retained for the period required under applicable laws.

5.3 Customers may request correction or deletion of their personal information, subject to applicable legal and record-retention requirements.

 6. Cookies

6.1 Our website may use cookies and similar technologies to maintain login sessions, remember preferences, improve website functionality and understand website usage.

6.2 Customers can manage cookies through their browser settings. Disabling certain cookies may affect website functionality.

 7. Customer Rights

Subject to applicable laws, customers may:

- Request access to their personal information.
- Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.
- Request deletion of personal information where legally permissible.
- Withdraw consent where processing is based on consent.
- Raise concerns regarding the handling of personal information.
- Submit privacy-related complaints through our contact details.

### 8. Third-Party Websites

Our website may contain links to third-party websites, payment gateways and courier tracking platforms.

We are not responsible for the privacy practices or policies of external websites. Customers are encouraged to review their respective privacy policies.

 9. Children's Privacy

Our online ordering services are intended for individuals who can legally enter into transactions. Where personal information of children is processed, applicable legal requirements relating to children's data and parental consent will be followed.

10. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices, website functionality or applicable laws.

The updated policy will be published on our website with the revised effective date.

 11. Contact and Privacy Grievances

For questions, requests, corrections or complaints relating to personal information, please contact:

Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation

Email: care@vaidyagogate.org  
Phone: 8668904067  
Address: Gogate Memorial Clinic, 102, Ramprasad Chambers, 368/1, Nana Peth, Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Pune – 411002.

We aim to acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and resolve them within one month, subject to the nature of the complaint and applicable legal requirements.

Last Updated: 13 November 2026

Welcome to the online store of Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation. By accessing our website, creating an account, placing an order or making a payment, you agree to these Terms and Conditions.

Please read these terms carefully before placing a Normal Order or Pre-Order.

 1. Definitions

For the purposes of these Terms and Conditions:

1.1 Foundation: Refers to Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation.

1.2 Customer:Refers to any individual placing an order through our website.

1.3 Normal Order:Refers to an order placed for a book or product that is currently available in stock and ready for processing.

1.4 Pre-Order: Refers to an advance booking for a book or product that is not yet available for immediate dispatch.

1.5 Booking Amount:Refers to the advance amount collected to reserve a copy of a pre-ordered book. This amount forms part of the total product price.

1.6 Platform Fee: Refers to the applicable fee charged for facilitating and processing an order through our website.

1.7 Order Confirmation:Refers to the confirmation message or email issued by the Foundation after successful order placement and payment verification.

2. Product Availability

2.1 Product availability and stock status will be displayed on the respective product pages.

2.2 Normal Orders are subject to stock availability at the time of order confirmation.

2.3 Pre-Orders are accepted for books or products that are expected to become available at a future date.

2.4 The expected availability date of a Pre-Order will be communicated on the product page or through an appropriate customer notification.

2.5 For example, a book may be announced as available from the end of December 2026. Such dates are indicative and may change due to circumstances beyond our reasonable control, including printing, binding, manufacturing, supply or transportation delays.

2.6 We will inform customers of significant availability delays as soon as reasonably possible.

2.7 If a Pre-Order is delayed by more than 30 days beyond the announced availability date, the customer may cancel the order and receive a full refund, including the platform fee.

 3. Orders and Confirmation

3.1 Customers must provide accurate personal information, contact details and delivery addresses while placing an order.

3.2 Customers are responsible for checking the selected product, book language, quantity, price and delivery address before completing payment.

3.3 An order will be considered confirmed only after successful payment verification and receipt of an order confirmation message or email.

3.4 For Pre-Orders, confirmation is subject to successful receipt of the applicable booking amount.

3.5 Orders will generally be processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

3.6 For Pre-Orders, priority will be determined according to the date and time of receipt of the booking amount.

3.7 If payment has been made but confirmation has not been received, customers should contact our support team with their payment transaction details.

3.8 The Foundation reserves the right to cancel an order in cases of suspected fraud, payment discrepancies, technical errors, product unavailability or other valid operational circumstances.

 4. Pricing and Platform Fees

4.1 Product prices will be displayed on the website at the time of ordering.

4.2 All prices are in Indian Rupees (INR) and include applicable taxes unless stated otherwise.

4.3 A platform fee may be charged in addition to the product price. The applicable fee will be disclosed before payment.

4.4 Shipping and packaging charges, where applicable, will be displayed or communicated before the customer completes the final payment.

4.5 The total payable amount will be calculated based on the product price, applicable platform fee, shipping charges, packaging charges and applicable taxes.

4.6 Any promotional offer, discount or free-shipping benefit will be subject to its displayed terms and eligibility conditions.

 5. Payment Terms

 5.1 Normal Orders

a. Full payment, including applicable platform and shipping charges, must be completed before dispatch.

b. Orders will not be dispatched until the required payment has been successfully received.

 5.2 Pre-Orders

a. A booking amount will be collected at the time of placing the Pre-Order.

b. The booking amount is part of the total price of the book and is not an additional charge.

c. Once the book becomes available, the customer will be notified.

d. The customer must then finalise the delivery method, including courier delivery, self-arranged courier collection or store pickup.

e. The remaining product balance and applicable charges must be paid before dispatch or handover.

f. For courier delivery, full payment, including applicable courier and packaging charges, must be received before dispatch.

g. For store pickup, the final payment must be completed before the book is handed over.

5.3 Payments are processed through third-party payment gateway providers.

5.4 We do not store complete credit card numbers, UPI PINs or banking credentials on our servers.

5.5 Customers should not share their OTPs, UPI PINs, passwords or other payment credentials with anyone claiming to represent the Foundation.

 6. Shipping and Delivery

6.1 Orders may be delivered through our available courier and logistics partners.

6.2 Customers may also arrange their own courier service to collect the book, subject to prior coordination with the Foundation.

6.3 Delivery timelines provided by courier partners are estimates only and are not guaranteed.

6.4 Customers must provide a complete and correct address, PIN code and working mobile number.

6.5 Delays or failed delivery caused by incorrect or incomplete customer details may result in additional re-delivery charges, where applicable.

6.6 Once the parcel is handed over to the courier partner, delivery and transit operations are subject to the courier partner's service conditions.

6.7 We will take reasonable care in packing products before dispatch.

6.8 Customers are encouraged to record an unboxing video when opening their parcels.

6.9 Damage, shortage or incorrect products should be reported within the applicable reporting period under our Return Policy.

6.10 Nothing in these terms excludes consumer rights or remedies available under applicable law.

7. Store Pickup

7.1 Customers may collect their orders from the following location:

Gogate Memorial Clinic

102, Ramprasad Chambers, 368/1, Nana Peth, Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Near Kirad Hospital, Above Shraddha Medical, Pune – 411002.

7.2 Pickup timings are:

Monday to Thursday: 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM.

7.3 Pickup is not available at other times or on other days unless separately confirmed by the Foundation.

7.4 Customers must carry their order confirmation and a valid photo ID.

7.5 For Pre-Orders, customers will be notified when the book is ready for collection.

7.6 Customers should collect the book within 30 days of receiving the readiness notification.

7.7 If the customer does not collect the book within 30 days, the Foundation may cancel the order and process the refund in accordance with the applicable Refund and Cancellation Policies.

 8. Cancellation Policy

8.1 Customers may request cancellation of an order before it is dispatched.

8.2 Once an order has been handed over to the courier partner for dispatch, cancellation may no longer be possible.

8.3 For customer-initiated cancellations before dispatch, the amount paid will be refunded after deducting the applicable non-refundable platform fee.

8.4 If the Foundation cancels an order or is unable to supply the product, the full amount paid, including the platform fee, will be refunded.

8.5 For Pre-Orders, if product availability is delayed by more than 30 days beyond the announced date, customers may cancel and receive a full refund, including the platform fee.

8.6 All cancellation requests are subject to review and confirmation by our customer support team.

 9. Return and Replacement Policy

9.1 Customers may request a return or replacement in eligible circumstances, including:

- Receiving an incorrect book or product.
- Receiving a book in a language different from the language ordered.
- Receiving a damaged or defective product.
- Receiving a product materially different from the one ordered.

 9.2 Wrong Book or Wrong Language

a. If the delivered book is in a different language from the language ordered, we will arrange a replacement at no additional cost.

b. Customers must notify us within 3 days of receiving the book.

c. Photographs of the received book and order confirmation must be provided.

d. The incorrectly supplied book must be returned in unused condition.

e. Return courier charges for incorrectly supplied products will be borne by the Foundation.

9.3 Damaged Products

a. Damage must be reported within 48 hours of delivery.

b. Customers are requested to provide an unboxing video and photographs of the product and packaging.

c. If damage is attributable to inadequate packing by the Foundation, an appropriate replacement will be arranged without additional product or shipping charges.

d. Where damage is attributable to courier handling, we will assist in coordinating with the courier partner and raising a claim wherever applicable.

 9.4 Non-Eligible Returns

Returns will generally not be accepted for:

- Products damaged after delivery due to improper handling or storage by the customer.
- Products returned without prior approval.
- Change of mind or incorrect orders placed by the customer.

These exclusions are subject to applicable consumer protection laws.

9.5 Pre-Orders

Once a Pre-Order has been dispatched, the same return and replacement conditions applicable to Normal Orders will apply.

Before dispatch, customers may request cancellation under the Cancellation Policy.

 9.6 Return Approval

All return and replacement requests must be submitted through the available website facility or customer support channels.

Customers must obtain approval and return instructions before sending products back.

The Foundation may inspect returned products before approving the requested refund or replacement.

 10. Refund Policy

10.1 Approved refunds will generally be initiated within approximately 8 working days after the cancellation or refund request is accepted.

10.2 Refunds will ordinarily be processed through the original payment method wherever possible.

10.3 Banks, UPI applications and payment providers may require additional time to credit the refunded amount.

10.4 For customer-initiated cancellations before dispatch, the applicable platform fee is non-refundable.

10.5 If the Foundation cancels an order or is unable to supply the product, the full amount paid, including the platform fee, will be refunded.

10.6 If a Pre-Order is delayed by more than 30 days beyond its announced availability date and the customer elects to cancel, the full amount paid, including the platform fee, will be refunded.

10.7 Shipping and packaging charges for successfully dispatched orders are generally non-refundable for customer-initiated cancellations or returns, except where required by law or where the issue is attributable to the Foundation.

10.8 Nothing in this clause permits any deduction that is prohibited by applicable law.

11. Copyright and Intellectual Property

11.1 All books, publications, photographs, illustrations, content and other intellectual property made available through our website are protected by applicable copyright and intellectual property laws.

11.2 No part of any book or publication may be copied, reproduced, scanned, uploaded, distributed, shared or commercially exploited without prior written permission from the respective copyright owner.

11.3 Purchased books are intended for personal use unless a different licence is expressly granted.

11.4 Purchasing a physical copy does not transfer copyright or ownership of the underlying intellectual property.

11.5 Unauthorised commercial reproduction, resale or distribution is prohibited, subject to applicable law.

 12. Medical Disclaimer

12.1 Books and publications offered through our website are intended for educational and informational purposes.

12.2 The information contained in such publications is not a substitute for professional medical diagnosis, advice or treatment.

12.3 Readers should consult a qualified medical practitioner before making medical decisions or undertaking treatment.

12.4 The Foundation does not guarantee any particular medical outcome from the use of information contained in its publications.

 13. Privacy and Personal Information

13.1 We collect personal information such as name, mobile number, email address and billing or delivery address for order processing and customer communication.

13.2 Personal information may be shared with courier partners, payment providers and necessary technology service providers for fulfilment of orders and operation of our website.

13.3 We do not sell customers' personal information.

13.4 Customers may request correction or deletion of their personal information, subject to applicable legal and record-retention requirements.

13.5 Further information is available in our Privacy Policy.

 14. Limitation of Liability

14.1 The Foundation will take reasonable care in processing orders, packing products and coordinating deliveries.

14.2 To the extent permitted by applicable law, our liability in connection with an order will be limited to the amount paid by the customer for that order.

14.3 Nothing in these terms excludes or restricts liability or consumer rights that cannot legally be excluded or restricted.

14.4 The Foundation shall not be responsible for delays caused by circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, transport disruptions, government restrictions and supply-chain interruptions, subject to applicable law.

 15. Changes to These Terms

15.1 The Foundation reserves the right to update or modify these Terms and Conditions from time to time.

 16. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

16.1 These Terms and Conditions shall be governed by the laws of India.

17. Contact and Grievances

Vaidya Gogate Memorial Foundation is committed to delivering books and other products safely and efficiently. This Shipping Policy applies to all Normal Orders and Pre-Orders placed through our website.

 1. Normal Orders

1.1 Normal Orders refer to books and products that are currently available in stock and ready for dispatch.

1.2 Orders will be processed after successful receipt of the full payment, including applicable shipping and packaging charges.

1.3 Orders will be dispatched on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to stock availability and payment confirmation.

1.4 Once an order is dispatched, customers will receive shipping confirmation and tracking details, wherever available.

2. Pre-Orders

2.1 Pre-Orders refer to books or products that are offered for advance booking but are not yet available for immediate dispatch.

2.2 The expected availability date will be displayed on the relevant product page or communicated to customers.

2.3 Payment of the booking amount reserves the customer's copy, subject to successful order confirmation.

2.4 Pre-Orders will be processed for dispatch once the product becomes available and the customer completes the remaining payment.

2.5 Customers will be notified when their pre-ordered book is ready.

2.6 Pre-Orders will be dispatched on a first-come, first-served basis, according to the date and time of receipt of the booking amount.

2.7 Availability may be delayed due to printing, binding, manufacturing, supply or transportation circumstances. We will communicate such delays as soon as reasonably possible.

3. Shipping Methods

Customers may select from the following delivery methods, wherever available:

- Courier delivery through our available courier and logistics partners.
- Store pickup from our designated pickup location.

 4. Shipping Charges

4.1 Applicable courier and packaging charges will be communicated or displayed before the customer completes payment.

4.2 Shipping charges may vary depending on delivery PIN code, parcel weight, dimensions and courier partner.

4.3 Free shipping, if offered, will be subject to the conditions displayed at the time of ordering.

4.4 For Pre-Orders, shipping and packaging charges will be calculated when the product becomes available and the customer finalises the delivery method.

5. Delivery Timelines

5.1 Delivery timelines provided by courier partners are estimates and are not guaranteed.

5.2 Actual delivery may vary depending on the destination, courier operations, weather, public holidays and other circumstances.

5.3 Customers must provide a complete and accurate delivery address, PIN code and working mobile number.

5.4 Additional charges may apply for re-delivery if delivery fails due to incorrect or incomplete address details or the unavailability of the recipient, subject to applicable law.

 6. Damaged or Missing Shipments

6.1 Customers are encouraged to record an unboxing video when opening their parcels.

6.2 Any damage, shortage or incorrect product must be reported within 48 hours of delivery.

6.3 Customers should provide photographs or videos of the product, packaging and shipping label.

6.4 We will review the complaint and assist in resolving the issue, including coordinating with the courier partner wherever necessary.

6.5 Where damage is attributable to inadequate packing by us, we will arrange an appropriate replacement.

Nothing in this policy limits any rights available under applicable consumer protection laws.

 7. Store Pickup

Customers may collect their orders from:

Gogate Memorial Clinic 
102, Ramprasad Chambers, 368/1, Nana Peth, Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Near Kirad Hospital, Above Shraddha Medical, Pune – 411002.

Pickup Timings: Monday to Thursday, 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM.

Customers must carry their order confirmation and a valid photo ID.

For Pre-Orders, customers will be notified when the book is ready for collection. Collection must be completed within 30 days of the readiness notification.

8. Contact Us

For shipping-related queries:

Email: care@vaidyagogate.org  
Phone: 8668904067  
Location: Nana Peth, Pune, Maharashtra, India.
